facts.text: I want to lose 10 pounds in the next two months.
I increased my squat weight by 5 pounds the week before I increased it by 10 pounds last week.
I am 5'8" tall.
I weigh 170 pounds.
I go to the gym three times a week.
I go to the gym on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays at 7 am.
On Mondays, I do treadmill running and elliptical training for 30 minutes.
On Mondays, I do weightlifting focusing on my upper body.
On Wednesdays, I take a yoga class at 8 am.
On Fridays, I do weightlifting focusing on my legs.
I want to focus on a combination of both weightlifting and cardio to reach my goal.
I have no physical limitations or injuries.
I am willing to commit to working out three days a week.
I have a question about the leg day on Fridays and squats.
I want to know whether I should focus on a specific range of reps and sets for squats to continue making progress.
I increased my squat weight by 5 pounds the week before I was able to increase it by 10 pounds last week.
I want to determine the warm-up set weight for squats as 10-15% lighter than my current 1RM.
I asked whether I should track my 1RM for each exercise or estimate it more simply.
I think I understand how to estimate my 1RM and calculate the warm-up weight.
For my squat warm-up set, I should do 1 set of 8-10 reps with a weight that is 10-15% lighter than my current 1RM.
For my squat warm-up, I should then do 3 working sets with my current 1RM.
I want to increase the weight by 2.5-5 pounds every two weeks or as soon as I feel I can handle more.
I have been trying to eat more protein-rich foods like chicken, fish, and eggs to support my muscle growth.
I have been tracking my water intake.
I am trying to drink at least eight glasses of water a day.
I am not sure if I am eating enough calories to support my workout routine.
I want help estimating my daily calorie needs.

squat warm-up 8-10 reps and 3 working sets
increase weight 2.5-5 pounds every two weeks
